Consider the following ANSI C program:

Which one of the following phases in a seven-phase C compiler will throw an error?
explanation:
Step 1: Lexical Analysis
The lexical analyzer breaks the source code into a stream of tokens. Keywords, identifiers, and symbols like int, main, Integer, x, and ; are all valid tokens. Therefore, no error is detected during lexical analysis.

Step 2: Syntax Analysis
The syntax analyzer checks whether the sequence of tokens follows the grammar rules (Context-Free Grammar) of the language. The statement Integer x; matches the structure of a variable declaration statement (type_specifier identifier;). The syntax analyzer cannot determine whether Integer is a valid type name; it only checks grammatical structure. Thus, no syntax error occurs.

Step 3: Semantic Analysis
The semantic analyzer performs type checking and checks symbol tables to ensure that types and variables are defined before use. Since Integer is neither a built-in type nor defined using typedef or struct, the compiler raises an undeclared type error during semantic analysis.

Hence, the Semantic analyzer phase will throw the error.
